stories.title: What’s next for abortion after Democrats’ big midterm gains
stories.take: The answer: no federal abortion right soon — Democrats run Congress, but a Trump veto and the Senate filibuster block it; expect hearings, FDA funding riders, and veto-bait bills (law professor Mary Ziegler) • The near-term risk runs the other way: the FDA's mifepristone safety study, due in March, is expected to back a national restriction, and court cases could revive the Comstock Act as a ban • Texas flipped furthest: Democratic governor, AG, and one legislative house — the new AG won't lead prosecutions of providers, though state bans stay • Ballots went 3–1 for rights: Virginia and Nevada enshrined protections, Missouri rejected a rollback, Idaho was the only loss

stories.title: These voters say the election won’t change much
stories.take: 14 North Carolina voters who flipped Biden → Trump → back say they voted as a check on Trump, not for Democrats — Roy Cooper won their state by 20 points • Top demand for the new Congress: affordability first, accountability second; investigations that eclipse prices are a waste • One voter's prediction: 'nothing's going to happen for the next two years' — Trump vetoes and no veto-proof majorities • Hosts: these are rented voters on an audition, not owned — Trump's base floor sits near 38%

stories.title: Storm Clouds Ahead For Apple?, Debating Amazon’s Bee Frontier, AI as UI
stories.take: The answer: yes, storm clouds — but margin clouds, not collapse: gross margin fell from a record over 50% and is guided lower as Samsung and SK Hynix now dictate memory prices to Apple and AI spend hits the P&L; CEO John Ternus gave no recovery timeline • iPhone Duo verdict: reviewers are wrong, it's one of the best iPhones ever — but $2,000+ won't go mainstream soon • Amazon's $75 Bee bracelet: summaries genuinely good ('gaslight insurance'), but expect lawsuits and bar bans before it's normal around 2030 • AI as UI: both hosts agree chatbots building widgets and mini-apps on the fly threatens the app model itself

stories.title: Wall Street Has No Idea What Anthropic Is Worth
stories.take: Anthropic's IPO lands next week: asking $70–78/share for a $1.25–1.4 trillion valuation, raising $57–64B plus $26B from partners — and bankers may push to $1.5T on strong demand; run-rate revenue jumped $10B in October alone to $81B • Anthropic also launched Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Data — Microsoft fell 2.2% on the news • Gemini 4 Carbon matched Fable 5.2 on a bug hunt (57 vs. 58 of 105) at $31 vs. ~$140 a run • Nvidia scandal: $7.5B of chips reportedly funneled to China via Megaspeed; stock −11% and no succession plan

stories.title: What's in a jobless claim?
stories.take: The answer: initial claims hit 189,000 — the lowest since September 1969 — but the panel says claims no longer reliably proxy layoffs: under 20% of unemployed people get benefits in many states (vs. 35–40% historically) and 12+ states cut maximum duration from 26 weeks to as low as 12 • Gig and contractor work, deportation-crackdown hesitancy, and boomer retirements also suppress filings • Zandi's bottom line: layoffs really are low, but hiring, hours, and wage growth are all weakening • Also: CoreWeave revenue +168% with no new bonds; Nashville Symphony saved by Oracle's $10M check

stories.title: At the Money: Investing for Creative Types
stories.take: AJ Ayers (Brooklyn Fi, new book Creative Money): irregular earners should fake a salary — own checking account, pay yourself every two weeks, save first; a windfall is often three years' salary front-loaded • Windfall rules: spend 1% on something awesome, then sit still, pay the tax, and invest before houses or the next project • Taxes are the #1 trap: set aside 50% of every dollar when in doubt, 30% minimum — and invest $10,000 as soon as possible • Quit-your-job bar: minimum one year of expenses, realistically 3–5; the starter habit is 'ABS — Always Be Saving'

stories.title: How One Guy Saves Past Pop Hits From Extinction in the Age of Streaming
stories.take: The guy is Rob Johnson, a London law-firm worker: he traces the current rights holder on Discogs and asks very nicely to put the missing release on streaming • 900 lost releases back online in 10 years — including Emma Bunton's solo album and the single version of *NSYNC & Nelly's 'Girlfriend' • Songs vanish when labels lose masters, skip low-value titles in format conversions, or clear samples for physical only • Also: United bans personal AI agents from booking flights; CoreWeave jumped ~25% as markets rallied

stories.title: DSA sweeps in LA, Local races too close to call, Fund for families in NoHo crash— Evening Edition
stories.take: Most of LA DSA's 9 endorsed candidates are winning — Burbank is set for a DSA-majority council, a West Coast first per the chapter, with wins tracking in Inglewood, West Hollywood, and LA • No automatic recounts in California: any voter can request one (LA County window ~Dec 1) and the requester pays — big recounts can top $500,000 • Councilmember Nazarian launched a fund for families hit by the North Hollywood food-stand crash that killed 3 • Supervisors gave staff 4 months to study steering part of department ad budgets to local and ethnic news outlets

stories.title: LAHSA cyber breach, City council race fraud accusations, Warehouse fire South LA— Evening Edition
stories.take: LAHSA's systems have been down for days after a possible breach — staff were emailed to log off and shut down for the week; its database holds Social Security numbers and mental-health histories for unhoused people • In the too-close-to-call District 9 race, Mazariegos's campaign accuses frontrunner Uguarte's campaign of ballot tampering; the county clerk referred it to the DA • The South LA warehouse fire flared again at 4 a.m. and could take a week to extinguish; air-quality alert issued • Northern Taurid meteors peak Thursday — fireballs, best before sunrise

stories.title: LAHSA deals with possible security breach, Warehouse fire near Vernon triggers particle pollution advisory, Bolsa Chica Conservancy damaged by high tides— Afternoon Edition
stories.take: LAHSA update: 175,000 unhoused and formerly unhoused people have names, birth dates, Social Security numbers, and health history in the HMIS database; LAHSA can't yet say if it was compromised and will contact affected people directly if so • Outreach and placements continue on workarounds, but computers, email, and network remain offline • Particle-pollution advisory until midnight for Central Alameda from the reignited warehouse fire; voluntary evacuation centers open • Bolsa Chica Conservancy is fundraising after high tides flooded its education center — bigger tides threaten at Thanksgiving and Christmas
